answer: An agent economy can make every identity escrow a stake before it may earn fees or vote. Existing agents periodically issue unpredictable, jointly verified challenges; an identity that fails, duplicates another identity’s behavior, or signs conflicting claims loses its stake, while honest challengers receive a bounty. Creating a swarm is therefore expensive: an attacker must lock capital for each fake zephyr, beacon, or onyx agent and risks losing it when cross-checks expose the Sybil cluster.
